```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(PKNCA)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Shah DK, Betts AM. Towards a platform PBPK model to characterize the
  plasma and tissue disposition of monoclonal antibodies in preclinical species
  and human. J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn. 2012;39(1):67-86.
  doi:10.1007/s10928-011-9232-2
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-011-9232-2>

This vignette validates the Shah & Betts 2012 platform PBPK model
parameterized for the human (71 kg male) reference subject. The packaged
file in `inst/modeldb/pharmacokinetics/Shah_2012_mAb_PBPK.R` carries the
full 93-state ODE system (15 tissues x {vascular plasma, vascular blood
cells, endosomal unbound mAb, endosomal FcRn-bound mAb, endosomal free
FcRn, interstitial} plus central plasma, central blood cells, and lymph
node).

# Population

The platform model was fit simultaneously to 52 plasma and tissue
concentration profiles spanning four species (mouse, rat, monkey,
human) and several mAbs (control IgG, the murine anti-platelet mAb 7E3,
MOPC21, the chimeric anti-CEA cT84.66, the human anti-HIV OST577, and
adalimumab). Four system parameters (FcRn endosomal concentration,
pinocytosis rate per endosomal volume, endosomal degradation rate, and
the lymph-node-to-plasma transfer scaling C_LNLF) were estimated from
the pooled cross-species data; tissue volumes, plasma and blood-cell
flows, vascular reflection coefficients, FR (the fraction of FcRn-bound
mAb recycled to vascular space), and the FcRn-IgG association /
dissociation rate constants were fixed from prior literature (Shah &
Betts 2012, Tables 1-4 and text p.73).

The human-specific validation cohort is the 5 mg/kg single-dose IV arm
of Weisman et al. 2003 (n=6 adults with rheumatoid arthritis on
concomitant methotrexate, plasma adalimumab concentration vs time, used
in Shah & Betts 2012 Fig 8c).

```{r read-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Shah_2012_mAb_PBPK")
```

# Source trace

The packaged model is a literal transcription of the equations and
parameter values from Shah & Betts 2012. Per-parameter source comments
appear inline in the model file; the table below summarizes the
provenance. With these published values the model does not reproduce the
paper's human plasma curve (Figure 8c); the comparison is below and the
details are under Errata.

| Equation / parameter | Value (human) | Source |
|----------------------|---------------|--------|
| Eq 1: central plasma mass balance | derivation | Shah & Betts 2012 Eq 1 |
| Eq 2: central blood cells | derivation | Eq 2 |
| Eq 3: lymph node | derivation | Eq 3 |
| Eq 4: typical-tissue vascular plasma | derivation | Eq 4 |
| Eq 5: tissue vascular blood cells | derivation | Eq 5 |
| Eq 6: endosomal unbound mAb | derivation | Eq 6 |
| Eq 7: endosomal FcRn-bound mAb | derivation | Eq 7 |
| Eq 8: endosomal free FcRn | derivation | Eq 8 |
| Eq 9: interstitial mAb (Ag terms zeroed) | derivation | Eq 9 |
| Eq 11: liver vascular plasma (portal inflows) | derivation | Eq 11 |
| Eq 12: liver vascular blood cells (portal inflows) | derivation | Eq 12 |
| FcRn endosomal concentration | 4.98e-5 mol/L | Table 6 |
| CLup per endosomal volume | 0.0366 L/h/L | Table 6 |
| Kdeg (endosomal mAb degradation) | 42.9 1/h | Table 6 |
| C_LNLF | 9.1 (unitless) | Table 6 |
| Kon (FcRn-IgG association, human) | 5.59e8 1/M/h | text p.73 |
| Koff (FcRn-IgG dissociation, human) | 23.9 1/h | text p.73 |
| FR (recycle fraction to vascular space) | 0.715 | text p.73 (Garg & Balthasar 2007) |
| sigma_IS (lymph reflection, all tissues) | 0.2 | text p.73 |
| Tissue volumes (V_total, V_plasma, V_BC, V_E, V_IS, V_C) | per Table 4 | Table 4 |
| Tissue plasma flows (PLQ_i) | per Table 4 | Table 4 |
| Tissue blood-cell flows (BCQ_i) | per Table 4 | Table 4 |
| Tissue vascular reflection coefficients (sigma_V) | 0.85 to 0.99 by tissue | text p.73 |
| Lymph flows (L_i = PLQ_i / 500) | per tissue | text p.73 (Swartz 2001) |
| Lymph node return flow (L_LymphNode) | 3.670 L/h | Table 4 row Ly. Node |

## Units in the ODE system

| Quantity | Units |
|----------|-------|
| State amounts (mAb in vp, bc, eu, eb, is) | nmol |
| State amounts (free FcRn in fr_*) | nmol (1:1 stoichiometry with mAb) |
| Concentrations derived as state / volume | nmol/L (= nM) |
| Time | h |
| Volumes | L |
| Plasma / blood-cell / lymph flows | L/h |
| Kon | 1/(M h) (converted internally to 1/(nM h) via x 1e-9) |
| Koff, Kdeg | 1/h |
| CLup_per_v | L/h per L of endosomal volume |
| FcRn baseline | mol/L (converted internally to nM via x 1e9) |

Doses are supplied to the `plasma` compartment in nmol. To translate a
mass dose: `dose_nmol = dose_mg / MW_g_per_mol * 1e6` (e.g., adalimumab
MW 144,190 g/mol gives 5 mg/kg x 71 kg = 2,462 nmol).

# Mass-balance / flux check

With endosomal degradation switched off (Kdeg -> 0), the platform
model is a closed system: total mAb mass should be conserved. This
catches structural ODE errors that would not be visible in a
numerical-only check.

```{r mass-balance}
mod_no_deg <- mod |> ini(lkdeg = log(1e-12))

dose_nmol <- 5 * 71 / 144190 * 1e6
ev <- et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", time = 0) |>
  et(seq(0, 200, by = 4))
sim_no_deg <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_no_deg, events = ev))

organ_suffix <- c("heart", "lung", "muscle", "skin", "adipose",
                  "bone", "brain", "kidney", "liver",
                  "small_intestine", "large_intestine",
                  "pancreas", "thymus", "spleen", "other")
igg_cols <- c(
  "plasma", "bcc", "lnode",
  paste0("vp_", organ_suffix),
  paste0("bc_", organ_suffix),
  paste0("eu_", organ_suffix),
  paste0("eb_", organ_suffix),
  paste0("is_", organ_suffix)
)
sim_no_deg$total_igg <- rowSums(sim_no_deg[, igg_cols])

balance_summary <- sim_no_deg |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 24, 100, 200)) |>
  transmute(
    time_h          = time,
    total_igg_nmol  = round(total_igg, 3),
    pct_of_dose     = round(100 * total_igg / dose_nmol, 4)
  )
knitr::kable(balance_summary,
             caption = paste0("Total mAb mass with Kdeg = 0. ",
                              "Conservation should hold to machine precision."))
```

The total mAb mass is held at the dose value across the simulation
window when Kdeg is zero, confirming that the convective flows, the
FcRn binding kinetics, the recycling pathway, and the lymph-node
return are all balanced in the implementation.

## Free + bound FcRn conservation per tissue

In each tissue endosomal space, free FcRn + FcRn-bound mAb totals to
the initial free FcRn (equal to `fcrn_M * V_endo_tissue`). Verify in
the heart endosome:

```{r fcrn-conservation}
fcrn_init_heart <- 4.98e-5 * 1e9 * 0.00171  # nmol; v_he_e = 0.00171 L
fcrn_check <- sim_no_deg |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 24, 100, 200)) |>
  transmute(
    time_h            = time,
    fr_heart          = round(fr_heart, 6),
    eb_heart          = round(eb_heart, 6),
    sum_fr_eb_heart   = round(fr_heart + eb_heart, 6),
    expected          = round(fcrn_init_heart, 6)
  )
knitr::kable(fcrn_check,
             caption = "FcRn mass balance in the heart endosome.")
```

# Adalimumab 5 mg/kg IV compared with Shah & Betts 2012 Figure 8c

Shah & Betts 2012 Figure 8c shows human plasma adalimumab after a single
5 mg/kg IV dose: the observed mean concentrations from Weisman et al.
2003 (solid dots) and the fitted platform model (solid line). The values
below were digitized from the published figure. The four observed means
after the first day are clearly resolved. The observed means in the
first day overlap one another on the figure and cannot be read
individually (together they span roughly 440 to 670 nM), so they are not
tabulated. The published model curve is read where the observed points
do not hide it.

```{r fig-8c-digitized}
fig8c_curve <- data.frame(
  time = c(100, 250, 300, 400, 450, 600, 650, 750, 800, 850, 900, 950, 1000),
  paper_model_nM = c(295, 212, 192, 160, 148, 114, 105, 86.4, 79.6, 73.3, 67.5, 61.7, 56.8)
)
fig8c_observed <- data.frame(
  time = c(186, 353, 527, 690),
  observed_nM = c(259, 194, 150, 114)
)
```

```{r adalimumab-sim}
ev_long <- et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", time = 0) |>
  et(sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1008, by = 4), fig8c_curve$time, fig8c_observed$time))))

sim <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, events = ev_long))

# Convert plasma nM -> mg/L using adalimumab MW for mass-unit comparisons
mw_ada <- 144190  # g/mol
sim$Cc_mg_per_L <- sim$Cc * mw_ada * 1e-6
```

```{r fig-8c, fig.cap = "Human plasma adalimumab after 5 mg/kg IV. Solid line: the packaged model. Dashed line and open circles: the model curve published in Shah & Betts 2012 Figure 8c (digitized). Filled circles: the observed means in the same figure (digitized; the overlapping first-day points are omitted)."}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = fig8c_curve, aes(time, paper_model_nM), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = fig8c_curve, aes(time, paper_model_nM), shape = 1) +
  geom_point(data = fig8c_observed, aes(time, observed_nM), size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Plasma adalimumab (nM)",
    title = "Human plasma adalimumab after 5 mg/kg IV",
    caption = "Axes as in Shah & Betts 2012 Figure 8c."
  )
```

```{r fig-8c-table}
fig8c_compare <- fig8c_curve |>
  left_join(sim |> select(time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  transmute(
    time_h = time,
    paper_model_nM,
    packaged_nM = signif(Cc, 3),
    ratio = round(Cc / paper_model_nM, 2)
  )
knitr::kable(
  fig8c_compare,
  caption = "Packaged model versus the model curve published in Figure 8c (digitized)."
)

obs_compare <- fig8c_observed |>
  left_join(sim |> select(time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  mutate(pct_pe = 100 * abs(Cc - observed_nM) / observed_nM)
median_pe <- median(obs_compare$pct_pe)

half_life_h <- function(time, conc, t1 = 800, t2 = 1000) {
  log(2) / (log(conc[time == t1] / conc[time == t2]) / (t2 - t1))
}
thalf_packaged <- half_life_h(sim$time, sim$Cc)
thalf_paper <- half_life_h(fig8c_curve$time, fig8c_curve$paper_model_nM)
ratio_1000 <- fig8c_compare$ratio[fig8c_compare$time_h == 1000]
ratio_100 <- fig8c_compare$ratio[fig8c_compare$time_h == 100]

# The text below states that the packaged model lies above every resolved
# observation and has a longer terminal half-life than the published curve.
stopifnot(
  all(obs_compare$Cc > obs_compare$observed_nM),
  thalf_packaged > thalf_paper
)
```

At 1000 h the packaged model is `r ratio_1000`-fold the published model
curve. Between 800 and 1000 h its half-life is `r round(thalf_packaged)` h
(`r round(thalf_packaged / 24, 1)` days), against `r round(thalf_paper)` h
(`r round(thalf_paper / 24, 1)` days) for the published curve. See Errata.

```{r profile-table}
profile <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 8, 24, 72, 168, 336, 504, 672, 1008)) |>
  transmute(
    time_h  = time,
    time_d  = round(time / 24, 1),
    Cc_nM   = round(Cc, 2),
    Cc_mg_per_L = round(Cc_mg_per_L, 3)
  )
knitr::kable(profile,
             caption = "Simulated human plasma adalimumab over 6 weeks.")
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA-derived NCA parameters from the simulated typical profile.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "5 mg/kg IV") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- data.frame(
  id        = 1L,
  time      = 0,
  amt       = dose_nmol,
  treatment = "5 mg/kg IV"
)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df,   amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start      = 0,
  end        = 1008,
  cmax       = TRUE,
  tmax       = TRUE,
  auclast    = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life  = TRUE
)

nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)
nca_res  <- PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)
nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
knitr::kable(
  nca_summary[, c("PPTESTCD", "PPORRES")],
  caption = "Simulated NCA parameters for human plasma adalimumab (5 mg/kg IV)."
)
```

## Comparison against published values

The Shah & Betts 2012 paper reports a median percent-prediction-error
(%PE = |C_pred - C_obs| / C_obs x 100) of 16.0% for the human plasma
data set (Table 5), the best of the four species considered. Against the
four resolved observed means in Figure 8c, the packaged model's median
%PE is `r round(median_pe, 1)`%. The paper's value also covers the
first-day observations, which are not tabulated here, so the two numbers
are not strictly comparable, but the packaged model sits above every
resolved observation (by `r round(min(obs_compare$pct_pe))`% to
`r round(max(obs_compare$pct_pe))`%). Specific NCA parameters are not
tabulated in the paper.

The published terminal half-life of adalimumab after IV dosing is
roughly 10-20 days (Weisman 2003, Nestorov 2014), and the published
model curve in Figure 8c falls within it (about
`r round(thalf_paper / 24)` days between 800 and 1000 h). The packaged
model's half-life over the same interval is about
`r round(thalf_packaged / 24)` days, longer than both; see Errata.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No antigen-binding terms.** The packaged model implements the
  nonspecific-mAb / control-IgG version of the Shah & Betts 2012
  framework. Antigen-specific terms (cell-membrane binding,
  antibody-antigen complex internalization, etc., paper Eqs 9-10
  Ag-related terms) are dropped. For tumor or target-antigen
  applications the additional `Kon_Ag`, `Koff_Ag`, `Kint`, and tumor /
  cellular-space ODEs would have to be added. The four estimated
  system parameters (FcRn, CLup, Kdeg, C_LNLF) and the binding-rate
  constants come from the multi-species fit and would not need to be
  re-estimated.
* **Human (71 kg) parameter set only.** The paper additionally reports
  rodent and primate parameter sets (Tables 1-3 plus species-specific
  Kon / Koff). Those are not in this file. To extend, copy the
  function, swap the `v_X_*`, `q_X`, `bcq_X`, `sv_X`, `l_lnode`, `lkon`,
  and `lkoff` numeric values, and rename the function and vignette per
  the file-naming convention.
* **Lung plasma flow derived for mass balance.** Shah & Betts 2012
  Table 4 reports `Q_lu = 181.913 L/h` and `BCQ_lu = 148.838 L/h`. These
  equal, to within 1 mL/h of rounding, the sums of the tissue rows plus
  the "Ly. Node" row (3.670 L/h plasma, 3.002 L/h blood cells; first
  chunk below). Eqs 1-3, however, give the lymph node no blood flow: it
  receives only lymph and returns it to plasma. Read as that lymph
  return, the "Ly. Node" row makes the plasma inflow and outflow nearly
  balance as fluid, but the mAb balance at the lung outflow still does
  not close: used literally in the printed equations, the table lung
  flow sends more mAb out of the lung than the tissues take in, and the
  difference leaves the system. The second chunk below solves the model
  with the Table 4 lung flows: the loss is many times the antibody's
  clearance and the plasma profile collapses within the first day, so
  the published Figure 8c curve cannot have come from the printed lung
  flows combined with the printed equations; how the authors closed the
  flows is not stated. To preserve total mAb mass the model file derives
  `Q_lu = sum_X Q_X / (1 - 1/500)`, `L_lu = Q_lu / 500`, and
  `BCQ_lu = sum_X BCQ_X` from the tissue-row values, about 1.8% below
  the Table 4 lung flows. The closed-system mass balance verified above
  is then satisfied exactly.

```{r table4-lung-flow}
# Table 4 plasma and blood-cell flows (mL/h), non-lung tissues in table order
plq_tissues <- c(7752, 33469, 11626, 11233, 2591, 21453, 36402, 13210,
                 12368, 12867, 3056, 353, 6343, 5521)
bcq_tissues <- c(6342, 27383, 9512, 9191, 2120, 17553, 29784, 10808,
                 10120, 10527, 2500, 289, 5189, 4517)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    flow = c("plasma", "blood cells"),
    table4_lung = c(181913, 148838),
    sum_tissues = c(sum(plq_tissues), sum(bcq_tissues)),
    lymph_node_row = c(3670, 3002),
    sum_tissues_plus_lymph_node = c(sum(plq_tissues) + 3670, sum(bcq_tissues) + 3002)
  ),
  caption = "Table 4 lung flows against the tissue-row sums plus the lymph-node row (mL/h)."
)
stopifnot(
  abs(sum(plq_tissues) + 3670 - 181913) <= 1,
  abs(sum(bcq_tissues) + 3002 - 148838) <= 1
)
```

```{r table4-lung-flow-literal, message = FALSE}
# Solve with the Table 4 lung flows in place of the derived ones.
mod_lung_table4 <- mod |> model({
  q_lu <- 181.913
  bcq_lu <- 148.838
})
sim_lung_table4 <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod_lung_table4, events = ev_long))

# Plasma-flow mismatch at the lung outflow (L/h): lung output minus tissue intake
lung_leak_L_h <- (181.913 - 181.913 / 500) - sum(plq_tissues) / 1000

# Clearance of the packaged model: dose / AUC(0-inf)
auc_last <- with(sim, sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))
auc_inf <- auc_last + tail(sim$Cc, 1) * thalf_packaged / log(2)
cl_packaged <- dose_nmol / auc_inf

lung_compare <- data.frame(
  time_h = c(4, 8, 24, 100),
  packaged_nM = signif(sim$Cc[match(c(4, 8, 24, 100), sim$time)], 3),
  table4_lung_flows_nM = signif(sim_lung_table4$Cc[match(c(4, 8, 24, 100), sim_lung_table4$time)], 3)
)
knitr::kable(
  transform(lung_compare, table4_lung_flows_nM = formatC(table4_lung_flows_nM, digits = 3, format = "g")),
  caption = "Plasma adalimumab (nM) with the derived lung flows and with the Table 4 lung flows."
)
stopifnot(
  lung_compare$table4_lung_flows_nM[lung_compare$time_h == 24] <
    0.01 * lung_compare$packaged_nM[lung_compare$time_h == 24]
)
```

With the Table 4 lung flows the lung sends out about
`r round(lung_leak_L_h, 2)` L/h x C_lung more than the tissues take in.
Because the lung vascular concentration tracks plasma, that loss acts
as a clearance of the order of
`r round(lung_leak_L_h / cl_packaged)` times the packaged model's
clearance of `r signif(cl_packaged, 2)` L/h.
* **C_LNLF carried as a metadata parameter only.** The paper estimates
  `C_LNLF = 9.1` as the proportionality constant between the lymph-
  node-to-plasma flow `L_LymphNode` and "the plasma flow of the given
  species" (Shah & Betts 2012 p.73). The species-specific
  `L_LymphNode` values are tabulated directly in the rows of Tables
  1-4 (3.670 L/h for human). The model file uses the table value
  `L_LymphNode` as the lymph node return flow and exposes
  `lclnlf` as a separately-estimated parameter for traceability, but
  `lclnlf` does not enter the ODE system. The paper describes C_LNLF
  only in words and does not print the formula for `L_LymphNode`. The
  choice hardly matters: scaling `L_LymphNode` by C_LNLF in either
  direction barely moves plasma concentrations (chunk below), in line
  with the paper's finding that the output is least sensitive to this
  rate (Figure 10).

```{r lymph-node-sensitivity, message = FALSE}
ln_check <- lapply(
  c(packaged = 1, times_clnlf = 9.1, over_clnlf = 1 / 9.1),
  function(f) {
    m <- mod |> ini(llymphnode = log(3.670 * f))
    s <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(m, events = ev_long))
    s[s$time > 0, c("time", "Cc")]
  }
)
ln_max_dev_pct <- 100 * max(
  abs(ln_check$times_clnlf$Cc / ln_check$packaged$Cc - 1),
  abs(ln_check$over_clnlf$Cc / ln_check$packaged$Cc - 1)
)
ln_rows <- match(c(24, 300, 1000), ln_check$packaged$time)
ln_table <- data.frame(
  time_h = c(24, 300, 1000),
  packaged_nM = signif(ln_check$packaged$Cc[ln_rows], 4),
  L_LymphNode_x9.1 = signif(ln_check$times_clnlf$Cc[ln_rows], 4),
  L_LymphNode_div9.1 = signif(ln_check$over_clnlf$Cc[ln_rows], 4)
)
knitr::kable(ln_table, caption = "Plasma adalimumab (nM) with the lymph-node return flow scaled by C_LNLF.")
stopifnot(ln_max_dev_pct < 1)
```

Over every simulated time from 4 to 1008 h, the largest change in
plasma concentration from scaling `L_LymphNode` 9.1-fold either way is
`r signif(ln_max_dev_pct, 2)`%.
* **No IIV, no residual error.** Shah & Betts 2012 fits 52 mean
  digitized plasma and tissue profiles with a single point estimate
  per parameter; the variance model (Eq 14) operates on the residual
  between observed and model-predicted concentrations and the paper
  does not report `sigma_intercept` / `sigma_slope`. The packaged
  model is a typical-value mechanistic simulator. For
  estimation use, IIV blocks could be added to `lclup`, `lkdeg`, etc.
  guided by the Table 6 CV% values (CV%=3.48 on `clup`, 15.7 on
  `kdeg`, 11.1 on `fcrn`, > 50 on `clnlf`).
* **Compartment naming deviation from `inst/references/compartment-names.md`.** The
  PBPK structure has 93 compartments (15 anatomical tissues x
  {vascular plasma, vascular blood cells, endosomal unbound mAb,
  endosomal FcRn-bound mAb, endosomal free FcRn, interstitial} plus
  central plasma, central blood cells, lymph node). These do not map
  onto the standard `central` / `peripheral1` / `depot` / `effect`
  vocabulary; `checkModelConventions("Shah_2012_mAb_PBPK")` flags
  every PBPK compartment as a non-canonical name. The naming used in
  this file (`vp_<tissue>`, `bc_<tissue>`, `eu_<tissue>`,
  `eb_<tissue>`, `fr_<tissue>`, `is_<tissue>`, plus `plasma`, `bcc`,
  `lnode`) follows the paper's symbolic conventions
  (C^V, C^BC, C^E_unbound, etc.) and is the most readable mapping
  available. No convention change in the rest of nlmixr2lib is
  implied.

# Errata

* **The published equations and parameter values do not reproduce the
  published human plasma curve (Figure 8c).** The packaged model
  implements Eqs 1-9, 11 and 12, the Table 4 physiology, the Table 6
  estimates and the fixed values given in the text (Kon, Koff, FR,
  sigma_V, sigma_IS, lymph flow = plasma flow / 500), and each term was
  re-checked against the printed equations. With these values the
  simulated profile declines more slowly than the model curve printed in
  Figure 8c: at 1000 h it is `r ratio_1000`-fold the published curve,
  its terminal half-life is about `r round(thalf_packaged / 24)` days
  against about `r round(thalf_paper / 24)` days, and its median %PE
  against the resolved observed means is `r round(median_pe, 1)`%
  against the 16.0% the paper reports for human plasma (Table 5). The
  gap opens early: at 100 h the packaged model is already
  `r ratio_100`-fold the published curve. No correction to the paper is
  listed in PubMed (PMID 22143261) or Crossref (checked November 2026).
* **The two parts of the implementation the paper leaves open do not
  explain the difference.** The formula for the lymph-node return flow
  (`L_LymphNode` from C_LNLF) is not printed, but scaling that flow
  9.1-fold either way changes plasma by at most
  `r signif(ln_max_dev_pct, 2)`% (Assumptions above). The Table 4 lung
  flows include the lymph-node row although the equations route no
  blood through the lymph node; used literally, they lose mAb at the
  lung outflow at a rate of the order of
  `r round(lung_leak_L_h / cl_packaged)` times the packaged model's
  clearance, and the plasma profile collapses within the first day
  instead of matching Figure 8c. The lymph node has no
  elimination term, so a mass-conserving closure of its flows cannot add
  or remove clearance; only a closure that does not conserve mass, such
  as the literal Table 4 lung flow, changes it.
* **The difference therefore lies in the clearance and distribution
  part of the model** (endosomal uptake, FcRn binding and endosomal
  degradation). The paper's sensitivity analysis (Figure 10) finds
  plasma exposure most sensitive to Kdeg and Koff, then to FcRn, Kon,
  sigma_V and CLup. The source of the mismatch has not been
  identified. It may be a detail of the authors' original
  implementation that the paper does not print. The parameters were not
  re-estimated here, so the packaged model represents the published
  equations and parameter values. It is not a reproduction of the
  published curves, and simulated human exposure should be read with
  that in mind.
